exam.title: DBMS — Subject Drill 02
exam.subject: DBMS
exam.instructions: Subject drill. −0.25 for a wrong answer. Each question has up to 3 hints.

questions.q_en: Which normal form removes transitive partial dependencies on a non-prime attribute?
questions.hint: 2NF kills partial dependence. The next one kills transitive dependence.
questions.hint_2: Cross out 1NF (atomicity) and BCNF (every determinant is a key).
questions.hint_3: The surviving form is the one that forbids A → B → C when A is the key and C is non-prime.
questions.explanation: 3NF requires that no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on a candidate key. 2NF only removes partial dependence on part of a composite key. BCNF is stricter still: every determinant must be a candidate key.

questions.q_en: ACID: Atomicity guarantees that a transaction is
questions.hint: Think “all statements succeed, or none do”.
questions.hint_2: Isolation is “I”. Durability is “D”. This letter is “A”.
questions.hint_3: If one UPDATE fails, none of the UPDATEs in that transaction must remain.
questions.explanation: Atomicity means the transaction is one unit — every statement commits, or the whole thing rolls back. Visibility after commit is isolation/durability. Crash survival is durability.

questions.q_en: Which SQL command belongs to DDL?
questions.hint: DDL changes the schema, not the rows.
questions.hint_2: UPDATE touches data. GRANT touches permissions. COMMIT ends a transaction.
questions.hint_3: The leftover command can add or drop a column.
questions.explanation: ALTER changes table structure, so it is DDL. UPDATE is DML (rows). GRANT is DCL (privileges). COMMIT is TCL (transactions).
